about: Feeds the AI tested bars on every feature card and the 'Waiting for someone with the device' section of release-evidence.html. Rendered by tools/ai-tested.mjs. A bar is filled only from one recorded run's own count (passed of total). Nothing here changes a feature's percentage.

unitTests.how: Ran the sharing tests against the app's source code with made-up households: sharing switched off, on and unknown, the invite and stop questions, refused replies, and the guest preview. Not checked: real households, a real invite, an installed app, or playing shared media.

Ran the parental-control tests against the source code: the rating scale and presets, per-person Kids mode and layout locks, the PIN form and refusal handling, all with made-up data. Not checked: switching profiles in an installed app, real PIN enforcement, blocking playback, bedtime or daily limits.

unitTests.feature: Picture frame (photo wall for a tablet or TV)
unitTests.how: Ran the picture frame tests against the source code: off by default, the photo picker with made-up photos, creating and removing a frame link, link expiry and the schedule rules. Not checked: an installed PC, a real tablet or TV, scanning the QR code, or real photos.
Ran the Space Saver tests against the source code with made-up files only. Not checked: a real phone, real photos, or freeing real space.
Ran the home layout tests against the source code with made-up data only. Not checked here: the installed app (that is in the device records).

unitTests.feature: Music on the PC (library, mixes, desktop player)
unitTests.how: Ran the PC music tests against the source code with made-up music data only. Not checked: a real music library, the installed player, or sound.

Ran the reset and verification tests against the server source code with made-up accounts and pretend e-mail: both stay off unless switched on, and the reset and verification steps work with test data. Not checked: real e-mail delivery, live settings or real accounts. The feature is switched off.

Ran the rewards, credit and ad-callback tests against the server source code: each stays off unless switched on, no ad offers or rewards show by default, and a switched-off ad callback does nothing. Not checked: ads in an app, real purchases or live settings. The feature is switched off.
Ran the relay tests against the server source code with made-up data: the relay routes, the fallback and who may use it. Not checked: a real relay connection, real video, or a phone away from home.
Ran seven selected checks of the code that writes our name-server settings, with made-up input. Not checked: the live name servers or the live server.

Ran the Watch Together room tests for the PC side against the source code: handing over the host, buffering and rejoining, scheduled starts, host-only controls and clean-up. Not checked: the phone app, real phones, real playback in sync, or two homes.
Ran the PC-side Link a TV tests against the source code on a local test server: link expiry and removing a link. Not checked: the phone app, a real TV, pairing, or playback.
Ran the PC-side wake tests against the source code with made-up network adapters. Not checked: the phone app, sending a real wake signal, or waking a real PC.

Ran the PC-side collection, version and title-request tests against the source code. 64 passed. One check failed on purpose: it marks a known problem where a file name without a year can be read as a special edition. Not checked: the phone app or a real library.
Ran the PC-side library health tests against the source code with made-up files. Not checked: the phone app, the installed app or a real library.

unitTests.feature: Photos and phone backups (timeline, albums, viewer)
unitTests.how: Ran five Photos web tests on a local test server and 14 PC backup error tests against the source code: owner-only access, refusing requests that are not allowed, and handling backup failures. Not checked: a real phone upload, sync, or real backups.

Ran the PC-side podcast and radio tests against the source code with saved sample feeds: reading feeds and chapters, and checking radio requests. Not checked: the phone app, live feeds or stations, or sound.
Ran the PC-side audiobook chapter and naming tests against the source code. Not checked: the phone app, a real audiobook collection, or resuming on a device.

Ran 16 update and installer test files against the source code: version and download checks, the allowed download address, the publisher check, staging, retries, and the update-mode settings. 223 passed and 2 failed; the 2 failures were a timing problem in the test itself and passed when run alone. 2 tests were skipped.

Ran seven test files against the source code: headless settings, local network addresses and packaging checks. 2 tests were skipped because they need Linux file permissions. Not checked: a real Linux or Docker system, an installed server, or real files.
Ran two test files against the source code: Linux file names and packaging guards. Not checked: Linux itself, an installed app, or a package build.

unitTests.feature: Trip Journal link away from home
unitTests.how: Ran six test files against the source code with made-up data and a local test server: making a link, who owns it, limits and expiry. Not checked: a live link away from home, a signed-in account, or the installed app.

unitTests.where: our 6-core Windows test PC, imitating the Mac-only parts
unitTests.how: Ran four test files against the source code on Windows, with the Mac-only parts imitated: start at login, the Dock and menu bar icons, video acceleration choice through a pretend check, and packaging settings for Intel and Apple-chip Macs. Not checked: any real Mac or a Mac package.
Ran one small test file for line timing only (silence and gaps stay silent, lines stay in bounds). Not checked: editing, real speech, preview or export.
Ran the catalog test file against the source code: films and series shown the way Jellyfin apps expect, item ids, and the catalog cache. Not checked: a real Jellyfin app, sign-in, or playback.

extraRuns.feature: Android TV and Fire TV screens
extraRuns.how: An AI tester ran the app on the emulator with no sign-in: the first screen showed the sign-in code and QR for a phone; the remote reached every control with a visible focus box, and the language picker opened and closed; in the sample mode Home, Browse, Library, Play and More opened and search listed the sample clips; no crash.
extraRuns.notCovered: playing a video (the emulator could not show it), typing in search, seeking, subtitles, a real library, Fire TV, and any real TV.

tallies.feature: Opening the app and the five tabs

needsDevice.title: Waiting for someone with the device
intro: Most of these devices are not in our home, so we cannot try them ourselves. The code is written and, where a line below says so, it passed our checks on an emulator. An emulator is a program on a computer that pretends to be the device. It is not the real thing.
If you own one of these, please try it and tell us whether it worked. A real person on a real device is the only thing that can move these forward.
needsDevice.rule: Each line says what was run, on what, how many checks passed, and the date. “Not yet run” means exactly that. Nothing in this section raises a feature’s percentage. When a tester tells us they tried one, we add their result here with the date, whether it worked or not.
needsDevice.contactText: Tell Nick on the Become a tester page (tester Discord or e-mail)

rows.feature: Android TV and Fire TV screens
rows.deviceNeeded: A TV or TV box running Android TV or Google TV, with its remote.
rows.proven: On Nov 14, 2026 an AI tester installed the public 1.62 (134) on a real Chromecast with Google TV, verified its launcher and D-pad controls, and completed phone-approved linking into a populated Home. This is bounded real-device evidence, not person acceptance. Search activation, Browse clipping and season focus failed. The earlier private-emulator 4/4 record stays below.
rows.notTried: Fire TV, complete TV playback, subtitles, pairing expiry/removal and a complete remote journey. The recorded TV search, layout and focus failures still need correction and public-build retests.
rows.canTry: Yes. The TV app is inside the same Android test download as the phone app; you install it yourself.

rows.feature: Android TV and Fire TV screens
rows.deviceNeeded: A Fire TV stick, Fire TV cube or Fire TV television.
rows.proven: Built (a Fire TV version of the Android app). Not yet run on an emulator or a real device.
rows.notTried: Everything on a Fire TV: installing, signing in, the remote, and playing a video.
rows.canTry: Yes, as an in-development tester build.

rows.deviceNeeded: A Roku player or Roku TV in developer mode (Roku’s own setting for installing test channels).
rows.proven: Built. Our automatic code checks for the Roku channel passed 499 of 499 on Oct 2, 2026, on a computer, not on a Roku. Our notes mention one earlier short run in a Roku simulator made by another company, but it has no recorded count or date, so we do not count it. Not yet tried on a real Roku.
rows.emulatorNote: An earlier simulator run has no recorded count or date, so it is not counted.
rows.notTried: Installing the channel on a real Roku, signing in, the remote, and playing a video.
rows.canTry: Yes, as an in-development tester channel.

rows.deviceNeeded: An LG TV with webOS in Developer Mode (LG’s own setting for installing test apps).
rows.proven: Built. Our automatic code checks for the Samsung and LG TV app passed 252 of 252 on Oct 2, 2026, on a computer. The app has also been opened in a desktop Chrome browser. Not yet run on an emulator or a real device.
rows.notTried: Installing on a real LG TV, the remote, playing a video, and captions.
rows.canTry: Yes, as an in-development tester app, or you can try the TV’s own web browser.

rows.status: In development (iPhone and iPad apps); the web player in Safari is not yet tested
rows.deviceNeeded: An iPhone or iPad with Safari, and a Windows PC running Beebo that you can reach.
rows.proven: The web player has been checked in Chrome on Windows and on Android phones, not in Safari. The iPhone and iPad apps are written but have never run. Not yet run on an emulator or a real device (an iPhone simulator needs a Mac).
rows.notTried: Watching a film in Safari on an iPhone or iPad, adding Beebo to the Home Screen, and AirPlay to an Apple TV.
rows.canTry: Yes for the web player: open your Beebo address in Safari. Not for the apps: there is nothing to download yet.

rows.deviceNeeded: A Mac, with an Apple chip or an Intel chip.
rows.proven: Built. Our automatic code checks for the Mac parts passed 39 of 39 on Nov 8, 2026, on a Windows PC that imitates the Mac-only parts. Not yet run on an emulator or a real device.
rows.notTried: Installing, starting, scanning a library and playing a film on a real Mac.
rows.canTry: Not yet: there is no Mac download. If you have a Mac and would like to help once there is one, tell us.

rows.deviceNeeded: An Xbox in Developer Mode (Microsoft’s own setting for installing test apps).
rows.proven: Written, not yet packaged. On Nov 10, 2026, 36 of 36 of our automatic code checks for the Xbox app passed on a Windows PC. The full Xbox package could not be built yet, because a build tool is missing on our PC. Not yet run on an emulator or a real device.
rows.canTry: Not yet: there is no Xbox download. If you have an Xbox and would like to help once there is one, tell us.
